content.comment_body: Hello team, After programming my [product_name], I’m unable to halt program execution using the Esc button on the front panel. Connecting a PC with [product_name] software allows me to stop the process, but direct access from the device does not work. When Esc is pressed, the display appears to freeze while the program continues running in the background. If Esc is pressed again, the display returns to normal. Is it possible my code interferes with Esc key functionality (since it uses keypad input during operation), or is there a setting affecting this? Thank you in advance. I checked for similar topics but didn’t find anything helpful. Sorry if I overlooked something.

Hi, If you use text message blocks in your program code, try using the down cursor on the front panel to enter the input and output status menu. Then, press Esc to return to the main menu. Hopefully, this will help you.
Thank you for your suggestion. Navigating with the down cursor key until reaching the Time and Date Display, and then pressing ESC, successfully accesses the correct menu to stop the process.

analysis.insight_summary: A user observed that the ESC key on the front panel of the [product_name] does not immediately stop execution; instead, it only freezes the display while the program keeps running in the background. The solution involves navigating the menu with cursor keys before ESC can halt the process, revealing an unintuitive stopping procedure that may confuse users.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects that pressing the ESC key on the front panel should instantly stop program execution, without the need for further menu navigation.
